chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Umar ibn Hanzala who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two men from our companions who had a dispute between them regarding a debt or inheritance, and they both sought judgment from the Sultan (ruling authority) or the judges. Is that permissible?

So he said: Whoever seeks judgment from the Taghut and it rules in his favor, then he has only taken ill-gotten gains, even if his right was proven — because he accepted it by the ruling of the Taghut, and God has commanded that it be denied.

I said: How should they both proceed? He said: They should seek out the one among you who has narrated our hadiths, has studied our permissibles and our forbidden, and knows our rulings. Then accept him as an arbitrator, for I have indeed appointed him as a judge over you.

And when he judges by our ruling and it is not accepted from him, then it is God's judgment that has been treated with contempt and against us has been the rejection — and the one who rejects us is the one who rejects God, and he is at the boundary of associating partners with God.

key_terms.الشِّرْك: Shirk — associating partners with God; the hadith places rejection of the Imam-appointed judge at this level of severity
key_terms.حاكم: Hakim — ruler or judge; the Imam delegated this authority to qualified scholars
key_terms.حَكَم: Hakam — an arbitrator or adjudicator; in this context, a Shia jurist appointed by the Imam to resolve disputes
key_terms.سحت: Suht — ill-gotten gains; forbidden wealth acquired through impermissible means
key_terms.طاغوت: Taghut — an illegitimate ruling authority; in the Quran and hadith, refers to any authority other than God or His appointed representatives

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about seeking judgment from unjust authorities?
ai.summary: This is the famous 'maqbula' hadith of Umar ibn Hanzala, one of the foundational texts for the doctrine of wilayat al-faqih (guardianship of the jurist) in Shia jurisprudence. Imam Sadiq (AS) forbids Shia Muslims from seeking judgment from unjust ruling authorities (the 'Taghut'), even when their rights are legally valid, because accepting such a judgment through illegitimate channels nullifies its moral basis. In the second part, the Imam provides an alternative: seek a qualified jurist who has studied the Imams' teachings, and he carries delegated judicial authority — rejecting his rulings based on Imamic law is tantamount to rejecting God Himself.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Safwan, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Umar Bin Hanzala who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about two men from our companions who happened to have a dispute between them regarding a debt, or inheritance. So they went to the Sultan (ruling authority) for judgement, or to the judge. Is that permissible?’

So heasws said: ‘The one who goes for a judgement to the tyrant, so he judges for him, so he has rather taken ill-gotten gains, even if it was his right, proved, because he has taken it by a judgement of the tyrant. And Allahazwj has Commanded that [4:60] though they were Commanded to deny him’.

I said, ‘How should they both deal with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They should look around to the one who was among them who has reported our<sup>asws</sup> Hadeeth, and has looked into our<sup>asws</sup> Permissibles, and our<sup>asws</sup> Prohibition, and recognises our<sup>asws</sup> judgements. So they should present to him for the judgement, for I<sup>asws</sup> have made him to be a judge over you.

So when he judges by ourasws judgements, and it is not accepted from him, so rather it is the Judgement of Allahazwj which has been taken lightly, and against usasws is the rejection, and the rejection against usasws is the rejection against Allahazwj, and he (the rejecter) would be upon a legal penalty (Hadd) of the association with Allahazwj’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Safwan from Dawud ibn al- Haseen from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about two of our people who have a dispute over a certain issue of religion or inheritance, and they go for judgment before the Sultan or a judge; if it is lawful.

He (the Imam) said, ‘Whoever seeks judgment before al-Taghut (transgressors) who judges for him, whatever he then receives by such judgment is al-suht (sinful earning) even if it is his established right; he has taken it through the judgment of al-Taghut (transgressors) when Allah has commanded to reject al-Taghut.’

I then asked, ’What then should they do?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must find one among you who narrates our Hadith and has given thought about our lawful and unlawful matters and has learned our rules; then you must accept him as the judge among you; I have made him the judge and ruler over you.
When he issues judgments according to our rules and it is not accepted from him, then the rule and laws of Allah are taken lightly and our rules are rejected.
Those who reject us, they have rejected Allah and that is like taking things as partners of Allah.’”
